title: What is blockchain?
examples: How is a blockchain different from a regular database?
Can you explain what a 'hash' means in simple terms?
What kind of data can actually be stored on a blockchain?

explain.say: A blockchain is like a shared digital record book for many people.
Information is grouped into digital containers called blocks.
Each new block is linked to the one before it using a unique digital fingerprint called a hash.
This linking makes the ledger permanent because changing one block changes all subsequent hashes.

items: Block A (Original) -> Block B (Original) -> Block C (Original)
Block A (Changed) -> Block B (Invalid) -> Block C (Invalid)

draw.text: Change one block, break the chain

explain.say: Some uses include tracking supply chains or recording medical records securely.
A limit is that blockchains are not always fast for very high transaction volumes.

items: Speed | Can be slow under high load

faq.q: What is a hash function in blockchain?
faq.a: A hash function takes any input data and produces a fixed-size, unique string of characters. It is like a digital fingerprint for the data.
asks: How do hashes work in crypto?

faq.a: Decentralization means no single person or group controls the entire ledger. This is a key feature that makes it robust.

faq.q: Can blockchains store photos or videos?
faq.a: Blockchains are better for storing records of ownership or transactions, not large files themselves. They usually store a pointer to the file.
asks: What kind of data fits best?

faq.q: What is the difference between public and private blockchains?
faq.a: Public blockchains are visible to everyone, while private blockchains are restricted to members of a specific organization.

faq.q: Does immutability mean the data can never be changed?
faq.a: It means that changing data is computationally extremely difficult and would require controlling most of the network.
asks: How hard is it to tamper with?

facts: A blockchain is a distributed ledger technology.
Blocks are cryptographically linked in a chain.
Hashing creates a unique digital fingerprint for data.
Immutability means records cannot be altered easily.

quiz.say: If you change one word in a block, what happens to that block's hash?

options.show: The hash will only change slightly.
options.say: The hash will only change slightly.

quiz.why: The hash is mathematically dependent on all the data inside the block, so any change breaks the fingerprint.

wrong.0: This is incorrect; the hash function generates a specific, complex string, not just zero.
wrong.2: This is tempting because small changes seem small, but cryptographic hashes are extremely sensitive.
wrong.3: This is wrong because the hash is the core security element linking the blocks together.

quiz.say: What is the primary purpose of linking blocks using hashes?

options.show: To create an unchangeable, chronological record.
options.say: To create an unchangeable, chronological record.

options.show: To make the data look more complicated.
options.say: To make the data look more complicated.

options.show: To make the ledger faster to read.
options.say: To make the ledger faster to read.

options.show: To prevent people from seeing the data.
options.say: To prevent people from seeing the data.

quiz.why: The link to the previous block forces all subsequent blocks to validate the entire history.

wrong.1: While it is complex, the purpose is functional security, not just decoration.
wrong.2: The linking adds overhead; speed is often a trade-off for security.
wrong.3: Hashing secures the data, but the ledger itself is often designed to be visible.

quiz.say: Which characteristic makes a blockchain resistant to tampering?

options.show: The consensus mechanism across many nodes.
options.say: The consensus mechanism across many nodes.

quiz.why: Because many computers hold copies, an attacker must change the record on most computers simultaneously.

wrong.0: Encryption is used, but the consensus across nodes is the key to resisting tampering.
wrong.1: Larger blocks make things slower, not more secure against consensus attacks.
wrong.2: This describes a centralized system, which is the opposite of what makes it secure.
